stages.title: Planet Earth and its shape
stages.hook: If you could fly far up into space, what shape would you see Earth to be?
explain: Earth is our home planet. A planet is a very big ball that goes around a star. Our star is the Sun.
Earth is shaped like a ball. We say it is a sphere. It is a little bit squashed, but it looks round.
Earth is so big that the ground near us looks flat. A ship going away slowly seems to sink below the sea. That is because Earth curves.
Earth spins like a top. One spin takes a day. Where it is facing the Sun, it is day. Where it is facing away, it is night.

example.q: Is it day on all of Earth at the same time?
steps: The Sun can light only half of the ball at once.
example.a: No. When one side has day, the other side has night.

analogies.home: A ball in a room has a bright side near the lamp and a dark side away from it. Earth is like that with the Sun.
analogies.sea: A ship sails away and its hull vanishes before its sail. The sea curves like a ball.
analogies.sport: Earth is round like a football, not flat like a plate.
analogies.nature: A round orange has a skin. Earth has a thin skin of rock, too.

stages.mnemonic: Earth is a ball, round like a ball, spinning around.
terms: A big ball in space that goes around a star.
The star that gives us light and warmth.

misc.wrong: Earth is flat because the ground looks flat.
misc.right: Earth is so big that small parts look flat, but all of Earth is a curved ball.

stages.limits: Earth is not a perfect ball. It is slightly wider around the middle than from top to bottom.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures of Earth from space. What colours can you see?

questions.q: What shape is Earth?
questions.why: Earth is a sphere, a ball shape.

questions.q: What gives Earth light and warmth?
questions.why: The Sun is our star.

questions.q: When your side of Earth faces the Sun, what is it?
questions.why: The side facing the Sun is lit. That is day.

questions.q: What is a planet?
o: A big ball in space that goes around a star
A tiny rock that lies beside a road in the town
A soft white cloud that floats in the sky
A bright lamp that lights up a room
questions.why: Earth is a planet that goes around the Sun.

questions.q: Why does a ship seem to sink as it sails far away?
questions.why: Earth is curved, so the ship goes down behind the curve.

questions.q: How long does one spin of Earth take?
questions.why: One spin gives one day and one night.

questions.q: It is night where you are. What is true for the Sun?
o: Your side of Earth is facing away from it
The Sun has gone out for the whole night
The Sun has sunk down under the sea
The Sun is asleep behind the hills
questions.why: Earth keeps spinning. Your side has turned away from the Sun.

questions.q: Put these in order from smallest to biggest.
questions.why: A football is smallest, then a hill, then Earth, and the Sun is much bigger than Earth.

questions.q: Match each thing to what it is.
questions.why: Earth is a planet and the Sun is a star.

questions.q: Which shows that Earth is round?
o: A ship slowly disappears from the bottom up
Roads go straight on for a very long way
Hills are bumpy and go up and down
Birds can fly very high up in the sky
questions.why: The curve of Earth hides the ship little by little.

panel.q: You see the same Sun at the same time from all places on Earth. Is that right?
o: No, only half of Earth gets sunlight at once
Yes, the Sun lights up every part of Earth at once
Yes, because Earth is flat like a plate
No, the Sun only shines on the sea
panel.why: Earth is a ball, so one half is lit and the other half is dark.

panel.q: Why does the ground near you look flat?
o: Earth is very big and you see only a small piece
Earth is flat like a big round plate
You are standing on a huge table
All the hills are the same height
panel.why: A tiny part of a huge ball looks flat.

panel.q: If Earth stopped spinning, what would happen to day and night?
o: Part of Earth would stay in light and part in dark
Nothing would change at all for anyone on Earth
It would be day everywhere on Earth
It would be night all over Earth
panel.why: The spin brings each place into light and then dark.

teach.topic: Why Earth is a ball and has day and night
teach.model: Earth is a round ball in space. It spins, and the Sun can light only half of it. The half that faces the Sun has day. The other half has night.

points.ask: What do we get as it moves?

stages.title: Continents and oceans
stages.hook: Look at a picture of Earth from space. Is there more blue or more brown and green?
explain: Earth has big pieces of land. They are called continents. There are seven continents.
The seven are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America.
Earth also has big seas. They are called oceans. There are five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.
Water covers more of Earth than land. The Pacific is the biggest ocean.

example.q: How many continents and oceans are there in all?

analogies.home: Think of a big blue blanket with seven patches sewn on. The patches are continents and the blanket is the sea.
analogies.sea: A ship can sail from one ocean to another because the oceans join up.
analogies.sport: Seven teams play on a field of water: the continents are like the teams.
analogies.nature: Whales swim in oceans. Elephants walk on land.

stages.mnemonic: Seven lands, five seas: 7 and 5, that is how we say hi.
terms: A very big piece of land.
The icy continent at the bottom of the world.

misc.wrong: There is more land than water on Earth.
misc.right: Oceans cover about two thirds of Earth. There is much more water than land.

stages.limits: Some people count five or six continents because they join some together. Most schools say seven.

trip.prompt: Find all seven continents on the map. Which is the biggest?

questions.q: How many continents are there?
questions.why: The common count is seven.

questions.q: How many oceans are there?
questions.why: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic make five.

questions.q: Which is the biggest ocean?
questions.why: The Pacific is the biggest and deepest ocean.

questions.q: Which continent is cold, icy and at the bottom of the world?
questions.why: Antarctica is covered in thick ice.

questions.q: What is a continent?
o: A very big piece of land
A kind of big fish in the sea
A small pond in a garden
A tall tree in a forest
questions.why: Continents are the largest land areas.

questions.q: On Earth, what covers more space?
questions.why: Oceans cover about two thirds of Earth.

questions.q: A ship sails from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean. What does that tell you?
o: The oceans are far apart from each other
The ship flew over the land
questions.why: There is one connected world ocean.

questions.q: How many continents plus oceans are there? (7 continents and 5 oceans)
Match each place to its group.
questions.why: Asia and Africa are lands. The Pacific and Arctic are oceans.

questions.q: Order from the biggest to smaller. Biggest first.
questions.why: The Pacific is bigger than any continent. Asia is the biggest continent. Europe is smaller, and a pond is tiny.

panel.q: A globe is mostly blue. What does this tell you?
o: Most of Earth is covered by water
Most of Earth is hot, dry desert land
Land is much bigger than the sea
Earth is made of blue glass
panel.why: Blue shows water, and there is a lot of it.

panel.q: Penguins live in Antarctica. Why do we not find them on a hot desert?
o: They need cold places and sea
Deserts have no air to breathe
panel.why: Penguins are made for cold and for swimming.

panel.q: Which sentence is true?
o: Every continent is touched by at least one ocean
Some continents are far away from all of the water
Oceans are found inside the continents
There is only one continent on Earth
panel.why: Every continent has a coast on an ocean or sea.

teach.topic: The seven continents and the five oceans
teach.model: Earth has seven big lands called continents. It also has five big seas called oceans. There is more sea than land.

points.ask: What is a continent made of?
What is an ocean made of?

stages.title: Countries and cities
stages.hook: You live in a place with a name. What big groups of places are you in?
explain: A country is a land with its own name and its own people. It has a border. A border is a line between countries.
Each country has a capital. A capital is the city where leaders work. Kenya has Nairobi. Japan has Tokyo. Brazil has Brasília.
A city is a big place where many people live. A town is smaller. A village is smaller still.
You live in a village, town or city. It is in a country. The country is on a continent.

example.q: Your village is in Peru. Peru is in South America. Which is the biggest place in that list?
steps: Country is bigger than a village.
Continent is bigger than a country.

analogies.home: Your home is in a street, the street is in a town, the town is in a country. It is like boxes inside boxes.
analogies.city: A city has many streets, shops and schools. Many people live close together.
analogies.farm: A farm village may have only a few houses and fields.
analogies.nature: A small leaf is on a branch, the branch is on a tree. Places nest like that too.

stages.mnemonic: Home, town, country, continent: boxes in boxes.
terms: A land with its own name, people and border.
The main city where leaders work.
A big place where many people live.

misc.wrong: Every big city is the capital of its country.
misc.right: The capital is the city chosen for the government. It is not always the biggest city.

stages.limits: Some borders are not agreed by everyone. Maps may show them in different ways.

trip.prompt: Find your own country on the map. Can you spot its capital?

questions.q: What is a country?
o: A land with its own name, people and border
A kind of long road between towns and cities
A tall hill with a flat top
A small pond near a house
questions.why: Countries are places with borders.

questions.q: What is a capital?
o: The main city where a country's leaders work
The biggest shop in the whole town
A kind of boat that sails the sea
A school where many children learn
questions.why: The capital is the home of the government.

questions.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.why: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

questions.q: What is the capital of Kenya?
questions.why: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

questions.q: What is a border?
o: A kind of tree with thick bark
A fruit that grows on a tree
A river that runs to the sea
questions.why: A border shows where one country ends and another starts.

questions.q: Which place is the biggest?
questions.why: A continent holds many countries.

questions.q: Which is the smallest?
questions.why: Villages are small groups of homes.

questions.q: Order from the smallest to the biggest place.
questions.why: Each place sits inside the next one.

questions.q: Match each city to its country.
questions.why: These cities are the capitals of those countries.

questions.q: Is a city always the capital of its country?
o: No, many cities are not capitals
Yes, every single city is a capital
Only the big ones are capitals
Only the ones by the sea
questions.why: For example, Sydney is big but Canberra is the capital of Australia.

panel.q: A friend lives in Lagos in Nigeria. Which is bigger, Lagos or Nigeria?
panel.why: A country holds many cities, so it is bigger.

panel.q: Why do countries have borders?
o: To show where one country ends and another begins
To make the roads wet when it rains a lot
To hold up the sky above us
To help the trees grow tall
panel.why: Borders say whose land is whose.

panel.q: Brazil's capital is Brasília, but Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo are bigger. What does this show?
o: The capital is not always the biggest city
Brazil has no capital city at all
Rio de Janeiro is the capital city
Capitals are always the smallest cities
panel.why: Capitals are chosen for government, not size.

teach.topic: What countries, capitals and cities are
teach.model: A country is a land with a border. Its capital is the city where leaders work. Cities, towns and villages are places where people live inside a country.

points.ask: Which city do leaders work in?
How do we know where a country ends?

stages.title: Mountains and valleys
stages.hook: What is the tallest thing that is not made by people? How do you walk up it?
explain: A mountain is very high land. A hill is smaller. Some mountains have snow on top.
A valley is low land between hills or mountains. A river often runs through a valley.
A plain is wide flat land. Many farms are on plains.
Mount Everest in Asia is the highest mountain on Earth. Mountains are chains called ranges, like the Andes in South America.

example.q: A hill is 100 metres high. A mountain is 2000 metres high. Which one is taller?

analogies.home: A pile of pillows is a hill. A big pile of them is a mountain. The dip between two piles is a valley.
analogies.farm: Farmers grow crops in flat plains. Goats and sheep live on slopes.
analogies.sport: Skiers go up mountains. Runners may race along a flat valley road.
analogies.nature: Snow can stay on top of a high mountain even in summer, because it is so cold up there.

stages.mnemonic: Mountain up, valley down, plain flat all around.
terms: Very high land with steep sides.
Low land between hills or mountains.

misc.wrong: A valley is the top of a mountain.
misc.right: A valley is low land. The top of a mountain is called the peak or summit.

stages.limits: There is no strict height that separates a hill from a mountain. People use different rules.

trip.prompt: Find a photo of a mountain with snow. How does the top differ from the bottom?

questions.q: What is a valley?
o: Low land between hills or mountains
The very top of a tall, snowy mountain
A kind of lake with high banks
A road that winds up a hill
questions.why: A valley sits low.

questions.q: Which is the highest mountain on Earth?
questions.why: Everest in Asia is the highest above sea level.

questions.q: What is wide, flat land with no hills called?
questions.why: A plain is wide and flat.

questions.q: Which is usually the tallest?
questions.why: Mountains are higher than hills.

questions.q: What is a line of mountains called?
questions.why: The Andes are a range.

questions.q: Why is snow often on top of a high mountain?
o: It is very cold high up
Snow is made there by farmers
The sun is closer to it
questions.why: The higher you go, the colder it gets.

questions.q: Where would farmers find wide flat land for crops?
questions.why: Flat land is easy to farm.

questions.q: Order from the lowest to the highest land.
questions.why: A plain is flat and low, hills are higher, and mountains are the highest.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.why: These are words for parts of the land.

questions.q: Where do rivers often flow?
questions.why: Water runs downhill into low land.

panel.q: Water falls as rain on a mountain. Where will it run?
o: Up to the top of the peak
It stays still and does not move
Into the sky as a cloud
panel.why: Water always moves downhill.

panel.q: A traveller must cross a mountain range. Why might she choose a valley route?
o: The ground is lower and easier to walk
Valleys are covered in deep snow all year
Valleys are higher than the peaks
Valleys are made of slippery sand
panel.why: Low routes are less steep.

panel.q: Why are plains good for towns and farms?
o: The land is flat and easy to build and plant on
Plains are always very cold and icy places
Plains have no soil to plant in
Plains are always covered by water
panel.why: Flat land makes building and farming simple.

teach.model: A mountain is very high land. A valley is low land between hills. A plain is wide flat land. Rivers run down mountains and through valleys.

points.ask: What does water do on a mountain?

stages.title: Rivers and lakes
stages.hook: Where does the water in a river come from, and where does it go?
explain: A river is water that flows along the land. It begins high up, often on a mountain. It flows down to the sea.
A lake is water with land all around it. It does not flow away like a river.
The Nile in Africa is one of the longest rivers. The Amazon in South America carries the most water.
Rivers give us water to drink, to wash and to grow food. People must keep them clean.

example.q: Rain falls on a hill. The water runs into a stream, the stream joins a river and the river reaches the sea. Where does the water end?
steps: Streams join to make a river.
A river flows to the sea.

analogies.home: A bath tap is like a spring. The plug hole is like the sea. The water runs down the middle.
analogies.city: Many cities are on rivers, so boats bring goods and people.
analogies.farm: Farmers use river water to give plants a drink.
analogies.nature: Fish, frogs and birds live in and by rivers and lakes.

stages.mnemonic: River runs down to the sea, lake sits still like me.
terms: Water that flows along the land to the sea.
Water with land all around it.
Where a river meets the sea.

misc.wrong: Rivers flow uphill to reach the sea.
misc.right: Rivers always flow downhill because gravity pulls water down.

stages.limits: Some lakes are salty. Some rivers dry up in dry seasons.

trip.prompt: Follow the Nile on a map. Which way does it flow?

questions.q: Where does a river end?
o: In the sea or a lake
On the top of a mountain
questions.why: Rivers flow to the sea.

questions.q: What is a lake?
o: Water with land all around it
A river that runs very fast
A mountain with a flat top
A road that goes round a hill
questions.why: A lake is still water in a hollow.

questions.q: Which way does a river flow?
questions.why: Gravity pulls water downhill.

questions.q: Which river is in Africa?
questions.why: The Nile flows north through Africa to the Mediterranean.

questions.q: The Amazon is in which continent?
questions.why: The Amazon flows through South America.

questions.q: What is the source of a river?
o: Where it ends at the sea
A fish that swims in it
A boat that sails on it
questions.why: The source is the start.

questions.q: What do people use rivers for?
o: Making mountains grow taller and taller
questions.why: Rivers help people in many ways.

questions.q: Order the journey of a drop of water.
questions.why: Water goes from small streams to big rivers to the sea.

questions.q: Match each word to what it means.
pairs: Where a river meets the sea
questions.why: These are parts of a river and lakes.

questions.q: A town is built on a river. Why is that useful?
o: There is water close by and boats can travel
Rivers build houses for the people in town
The town gets lots of snow
The river stops the rain from falling
questions.why: People need water and ways to travel.

panel.q: A stream is too small to get to the sea. It flows into a bigger river. What does this show?
o: Small streams join to form big rivers
Rivers always start out at the sea and flow up
Water in a stream flows up the hill
Small streams never move at all
panel.why: Rivers grow as streams join.

panel.q: Why do people keep rivers clean?
o: Animals and people need safe water
Rivers like to be washed with soap
Dirty rivers are higher up the hill
panel.why: Pollution harms living things.

panel.q: A lake has no river flowing out. Where does some of its water go in hot weather?
o: It flows uphill to the mountain
It floats away to the Moon
panel.why: Heat makes water vapour rise.

teach.model: A river is moving water that flows downhill to the sea. A lake is water with land all round it. People use both for water, food and travel.

stages.title: Weather and seasons
stages.hook: What is the weather like today? Is it the same all year?
explain: Weather is what the sky and air are doing today. It may be sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy or snowy.
A season is a time of the year with its own kind of weather. Many places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
Some places near the middle of the Earth are hot all year. They often have a wet season and a dry season.
Earth is tilted as it goes around the Sun. That is why we have seasons.

example.q: It is hot and dry in March, and rains come in April. Which season starts in April?
steps: The weather changed from dry to rain.
A wet season brings lots of rain.
So April starts the wet season.

analogies.home: We wear coats in winter and shorts in summer. We follow the weather.
analogies.city: In a rainy city, people carry umbrellas.
analogies.farm: Farmers plant seeds in the rainy season so plants can grow.
analogies.sea: Sailors watch the wind and clouds before they sail.

stages.mnemonic: Spring grows, summer glows, autumn blows, winter snows.
terms: What the sky and air are like today.
A part of the year with its own weather.

misc.wrong: Every place has summer in June.
misc.right: When it is summer in the north, it is winter in the south.

stages.limits: Some places have two seasons, wet and dry, not four.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures of the four seasons. How does one tree change?

questions.q: What is weather?
o: What the sky and air are doing today
A kind of food we eat for lunch each day
A kind of map of a town
questions.why: Weather is the daily sky and air.

questions.q: How many seasons do many places have?
questions.why: Spring, summer, autumn and winter.

questions.q: Which season is usually the coldest?
questions.why: Winter is the cold time of year.

questions.q: What falls from clouds?
questions.why: Rain is water that falls from clouds.

questions.q: What do you wear on a rainy day?
questions.why: It keeps you dry.

questions.q: Some places have a wet season and a dry season. Why might farmers plant at the start of the wet season?
o: Seeds hate the sun and need shade
Rain is food for the houses
The wet season is the coldest time
questions.why: Rain helps seeds grow.

questions.q: In Australia it is summer in January. What season is it in Canada?
questions.why: The seasons are opposite north and south.

questions.q: Put the seasons in order, starting with spring.
questions.why: The seasons go round every year.

questions.q: Match each weather to what you see.
questions.why: Each word describes the sky and air.

questions.q: Which tells weather, not season?
questions.why: Weather is today. A season is a long time.

panel.q: Why do we have seasons?
o: Earth is tilted as it goes around the Sun
The Sun turns itself off for a little while
The sea moves up and down
panel.why: The tilt changes how much sunlight reaches each place.

panel.q: A girl in Brazil and a boy in Spain are on holiday in July. Which one is likely to wear a warmer coat?
o: The girl in Brazil, because it is winter there
The boy in Spain, because it is cold there then
They both wear shorts and sandals
Neither of them needs a coat
panel.why: July is winter in the south.

panel.q: In a hot place near the middle of Earth, why is there often only a wet and a dry season?
o: It stays warm all year, so rain is what changes
Snow never falls in any hot place on Earth
It is always night in those places
The Sun moves far away from Earth
panel.why: Warm all year, so the big change is rain.

teach.model: Weather is what the air and sky are doing today. Seasons are parts of the year with a kind of weather. Earth tilts as it goes around the Sun, so seasons change.

stages.title: Maps and directions
stages.hook: You want to find the park on a drawing of your town. What do you need to read it?
explain: A map is a drawing of a place seen from above. It uses small pictures called symbols. A key tells what each symbol means.
There are four main directions: north, south, east and west. A compass shows them. We write N, S, E and W.
Many maps have north at the top. If north is up, east is on the right, west is on the left and south is at the bottom.
A globe is a ball-shaped map of the whole Earth.

example.q: On a map, the school is above the park. Which direction do you go from the park to the school?

analogies.home: A drawing of your room from above is a map of your room.
analogies.city: A bus map shows stops and routes with colours and dots.
analogies.sea: Sailors use a compass to find north at sea.
analogies.tech: A phone map shows a blue dot for where you are.

stages.mnemonic: Never Eat Soggy Waffles: North, East, South, West, going round.
terms: A drawing of a place from above.
A box that explains the symbols on a map.

misc.wrong: North is always the way you are facing.
misc.right: North is a fixed direction. A compass can find it, whichever way you face.

stages.limits: A flat map must stretch the round Earth a little, so shapes and sizes are not perfect.

trip.prompt: Look at a map of a city. Find the key. What symbols can you spot?

questions.q: What does a map key tell you?
questions.why: The key explains the symbols.

questions.q: What is the opposite of north?
questions.why: North and south are opposite.

questions.q: What is the opposite of east?
questions.why: East and west are opposite.

questions.q: What does a compass show?
questions.why: The needle points north.

questions.q: When north is at the top, which side is east?
o: The left side of the map
questions.why: East is to the right.

questions.q: A map shows a place from where?
questions.why: Maps are drawn looking down.

questions.q: What is a globe?
o: A flat piece of paper with a map on it
questions.why: A globe shows Earth as a ball.

questions.q: Put the four directions in order going clockwise from north.
questions.why: Going round to the right: N, E, S, W.

questions.q: Match each direction to its short letter.
questions.why: Directions use short letters on maps.

questions.q: The library is left of the bank on a normal map. Which direction is it from the bank?
questions.why: Left is west when north is up.

panel.q: Why do maps use symbols instead of drawing everything?
o: Symbols save space and are easy to read
Symbols are a secret code for maps only
Drawing is not allowed on maps
panel.why: A key explains them so the map stays clear.

panel.q: You are lost in a forest. You have a compass. How does it help?
o: It shows north so you can find your way
It tells you what time it is in the forest
It makes the trees move away
It calls your friends for you
panel.why: Knowing north helps you choose a direction.

panel.q: A map says the shop is east of the school. You are at the school facing north. Which way do you turn?
panel.why: Facing north, east is on your right.

teach.model: A map is a drawing from above. Symbols stand for things and the key tells what they mean. A compass shows the four directions: north, south, east and west.

points.ask: How do you know what a picture on a map means?

stages.title: Natural and human-made environments
stages.hook: Look out of a window. What was made by nature and what was made by people?
explain: Natural things were not made by people. Trees, rivers, mountains and animals are natural.
Human-made things were built by people. Houses, roads, bridges and schools are human-made.
A place can have both. A farm has natural soil and rain, and also barns and fences built by people.
We should look after both. We keep nature clean and we build in kind ways.

example.q: Is a river natural or human-made? Is a bridge over it natural or human-made?
steps: So the river is natural and the bridge is human-made.
example.a: The river is natural, the bridge is human-made.

analogies.home: A garden has natural plants and a human-made fence.
analogies.city: A park in a city is green and natural. The buildings around it are human-made.
analogies.farm: The field and rain are natural. The tractor and barn are human-made.
analogies.sea: Waves are natural. A lighthouse is human-made.

misc.wrong: Only forests and mountains are the environment.
misc.right: The environment is everything around us. That includes towns, roads and houses too.

stages.limits: Some things sit in between. A farm field is shaped by people, but it still needs sun and rain.

trip.prompt: Find a picture with a city and a forest. Which parts are natural?

questions.q: Which is natural?
questions.why: Mountains form without people.

questions.q: Which is human-made?
questions.why: People build bridges.

questions.q: What is the environment?
o: Only the trees and the plants
questions.why: It includes nature and human-made things.

questions.q: What should we do with litter?
questions.why: Litter harms animals and places.

questions.q: Which is a natural thing?
questions.why: Waterfalls form by themselves.

questions.q: A farm has both natural and human-made parts. Which is human-made?
questions.why: Barns are built by people.

questions.q: Which pair has one natural and one human-made thing?
questions.why: A lake is natural. A road is human-made.

questions.q: Match each thing to its type.
pairs: A path built for cars and walkers
questions.why: Nature makes rivers and forests. People build bridges and roads.

questions.q: Order what happens when we build a house.
questions.why: Building has steps.

questions.q: Why should we plant trees in a city?
o: They give shade and fresh air for people and animals
Trees make the traffic in the city worse
Trees stop the night from coming
questions.why: Trees help the environment.

panel.q: A new road is built through a forest. What might happen to animals?
o: They get lots of new trees to eat
Nothing happens to them at all
They fly away to the Moon
panel.why: Building can change the places where wild animals live.

panel.q: A town wants a park. Why is that good?
o: People can enjoy nature close by
It makes the whole town dark
It stops all the building for ever
panel.why: Green places help people and wildlife.

panel.q: Which choice is kind to the environment?
o: Cut down every tree you see
panel.why: Walking makes less pollution.

teach.model: Natural things come from nature, like trees and rivers. Human-made things are built by people, like houses and roads. We should look after both.

points.ask: How do we look after places?

stages.title: Exploring the seven continents
stages.hook: If you could visit all seven continents, which would you go to first?
explain: Africa has deserts, rainforests and grasslands. Elephants and lions live there. It has the Sahara, a big hot desert, and the Nile.
Asia is the biggest continent. It has the tallest mountains and many people. Europe is small, with many countries close together.
North America has Canada, the United States and Mexico. South America has the Amazon rainforest and the Andes.
Australia has kangaroos and a big dry middle. Antarctica is icy and very cold. No countries are there, only visiting scientists.

example.q: Which continent has the Amazon rainforest, and which has kangaroos?
steps: The Amazon is in South America.

analogies.home: Seven rooms in a big house, each one is different. The continents are like those rooms.
analogies.city: A big city has busy streets. Continents have big cities too, like Lagos, Tokyo and Paris.
analogies.nature: Penguins live near icy Antarctica. Camels live in hot deserts in Africa and Asia.
analogies.sea: The oceans lie between the continents like water between islands.

stages.mnemonic: Seven lands to see: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America.
terms: The continent with the Sahara and the Nile.
A continent with many small countries.
The icy continent with no countries.

misc.wrong: All of Africa is one hot desert.
misc.right: Africa has deserts, rainforests, grasslands and mountains.

stages.limits: Each continent has many kinds of places. A short list never tells the whole story.

trip.prompt: Choose one continent. Find one animal and one landform there.

questions.q: Which is the biggest continent?
questions.why: Asia is the largest continent.

questions.q: Which continent is icy and has no countries?
questions.why: Only scientists visit Antarctica.

questions.q: Where is the Sahara desert?
questions.why: The Sahara is in northern Africa.

questions.q: Where is the Amazon rainforest?
questions.why: The Amazon is in South America.

questions.q: Where do kangaroos live in the wild?
questions.why: Kangaroos live in Australia.

questions.q: Which continent has the countries Canada and Mexico?
questions.why: Both are in North America.

questions.q: Which continent has France and Italy?
questions.why: They are in Europe.

questions.q: Match each place to its continent.
questions.why: These places are in these continents.

questions.q: Order from the coldest to the hottest place.
questions.why: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth. A forest is cooler than a warm grassland, and the Sahara is very hot.

questions.q: Why do so few people live in Antarctica?
o: It is extremely cold and icy
It is much too hot there for people
It has too many big cities
It has no sky above it
questions.why: The cold makes it hard to live there.

panel.q: A traveller wants to see a rainforest and the Andes in one trip. Which continent?
panel.why: South America has both.

panel.q: Why can Africa not be called all desert?
o: It also has rainforests and grasslands
It has no sand anywhere in the land
It has no land at all
panel.why: Africa has many kinds of land.

panel.q: Which continent has many different countries in a small space?
panel.why: Europe is small but has many countries.

teach.model: There are seven continents. Africa has the Sahara. Asia is biggest. Europe is small with many countries. North and South America have mountains and rainforests. Australia has kangaroos. Antarctica is icy.
